newsitem.title: INDIA: India should speed up oil sector reforms -analysts.
newsitem.headline: India should speed up oil sector reforms -analysts.

text.p: India needs a comprehensive energy policy to exploit domestic resources and must speed up deregulation and market reforms in the oil sector in order to be globally competitive, analysts said on Tuesday.

India, which launched an economic reform programme in 1991, set up an official committee which recommended phased reforms of the oil sector over a six-year period, but experts said things should be done in half that time.

"India needs a total energy policy focusing on optimum exploitation of domestic resources, especially coal and hydro (electricity)," Mehdi Varzi, director, oil and gas research, at British-based Dresdner Kleinwort Benson Securities Ltd, told a conference on oil in the capital.
Varzi said India must develop its hydro-electric and coal resources more extensively.
He said only 18 percent of India's total hydro-electric potential was being developed and just one percent of total domestic coal reserves were being exploited.
India has some 250 years of coal reserves against 20 years of crude reserves and about 23 years of natural gas, he said.
Varzi said decentralisation should be the bedrock of any energy policy and reforms should be based on the widest possible cross-party support.

"Energy price deregulation should be included as part of reforms. It will encourage inter-fuel competition and create price transparency," Varzi told the two-day international conference, being attended by more than 250 delegates.
He said India should maximise the use of domestic energy sources and avoid over-dependence on imported oil and gas.
Varzi said state-run oil companies, whose shares have been sold under a partial privatisation programme, should be restructured before further divestments.
He recommended that state-run Oil and natural Gas Corp should continue to emphasise domestic exploration.
He recommended a maximum period of three years for the deregulation of the oil sector.
"A slower process might play into the hands of opponents of reform and upstream and downstream reform should proceed at the same time," he said.
Varzi suggested scrapping the current method of state-controlled crude oil and product purchasing and called for the free import and export of all petroleum products instead.
He said vital subsidies should be targeted directly at the intended recepients and marketing should be opened up with strong supervision to avoid abuses.
Michael Wilcox of consultants Wood Mackenzie said deregulation would bring about fundamental changes in the oil sector but the pace and timetable of deregulation would be critical.
He said India's state-administered oil price mechanism was causing distortions in consumer prices, large subsidies on key products and a lack of competition in pricing.
